devdoc.author: Ritesh Kumar
devdoc.details: The vault is an 8x8 grid held in encrypted 64-bit masks: tile `y * 8 + x` is one bit.      Routes are public. Layouts, outcomes and gold balances are encrypted.

params.raidIndex: Position in the vault's raid list.

params.forStash: True for a loot scan, false for a trap scan.
params.scanIndex: Position in the scanner's list for this vault.

params.owner: Its owner, or address(0) for a house vault.

returns.mask: One bit per tile in the block.

params.config_: Game parameters. A wall across the grid takes GRID_WIDTH traps, so the trap        count must stay below it to guarantee a clean route exists.

createVault(bytes32[],bytes32[],bytes).details: Each position becomes exactly one bit, so the budget holds by construction and the      owner never has to prove anything about the layout. A shift wraps modulo 64, so every      value lands on the grid. Doubled-up tiles only waste the owner's own budget. If the      owner cannot afford the stashes they are created empty, since an encrypted balance      cannot cause a revert without leaking it.

params.stashTiles: Encrypted stash positions, exactly `stashCount` of them.
params.trapTiles: Encrypted trap positions, exactly `trapCount` of them.

returns.owner: The owner, or address(0) for a house vault.

raid(uint256,uint8[]).details: The tile a raider is caught on is included in `traveled`, tiles beyond it are not, so a      raid reveals at most one armed trap to the raider and nothing to anyone else. The outcome      is unknown inside the transaction, so a raider cannot simulate and revert a bad result.

params.route: Tiles from the bottom row to the top row, each touching the last.

returns.raidIndex: Position of this raid in the vault's list.

params.jam: Revealed jam mask of the raid.

returns.escaped: Whether the raider reached the end of the route.
returns.traveled: Tiles walked, including the tile a raider was caught on.

retire(uint256).details: The owner may retire at any time. Anyone may once the vault expired or is full, which is      the only way a house vault retires.

returns.handles: Traps, each stash, then jam, traveled, escaped and payout for each raid.

scan(uint256,uint8,bool).details: A caller who cannot afford the scan gets an encrypted `false`, because the encrypted      balance cannot revert. The scanned tile is public, the answer is not.

params.forStash: True to look for unlooted stashes, false to look for traps.

returns.scanIndex: Position of this scan in the caller's list for the vault.

params.clearValues: ABI-encoded cleartexts for `revealHandles(vaultId)`, in that order.
params.proof: The KMS decryption proof for those cleartexts.

devdoc.title: Snare

InvalidKMSSignatures().notice: Returned if the returned KMS signatures are not valid.

SenderNotAllowedToUseHandle(bytes32,addr.notice: Returned if the sender is not allowed to use the handle.

ZamaProtocolUnsupported().notice: Returned if the Zama protocol is not supported on the current chain

PublicDecryptionVerified(bytes32[],bytes.notice: This event is emitted when public decryption has been successfully verified.

Raided(uint256,uint256,address,uint8[]).notice: A raid ran. The route is public; the outcome is not.

Scanned(uint256,address,uint256,uint8,bo.notice: A scan ran. The scanned tile is public; the answer is not.

StarterClaimed(address).notice: A player took their starting gold.

VaultRetired(uint256).notice: A vault retired and its history became publicly decryptable.

VaultVerified(uint256,uint64,uint64[]).notice: Every raid of a retired vault was replayed against its revealed layout and matched.

GRID_WIDTH().notice: Tiles per row. Structural: one tile per bit of a euint64, so not configurable.

areaMask(uint8).notice: The 3x3 block of tiles around a tile, clipped at the grid edges.

claimStarter().notice: Grants the one-time starting balance, readable only by the caller.

constructor.notice: Deploys the game with fixed parameters.

createHouseVault().notice: Spawns a vault whose layout comes from encrypted randomness. Nobody has ever seen         it, including the deployer and the caller, and it is funded by the game.

createVault(bytes32[],bytes32[],bytes).notice: Builds a vault from encrypted tile positions.

getScans(uint256,address).notice: Every scan a player made on a vault.

goldOf(address).notice: A player's encrypted gold. Only that player can decrypt it.

hasClaimed(address).notice: Whether a player has taken the one-time starting gold.

raid(uint256,uint8[]).notice: Runs a route through a vault. The result is readable only by raider and owner.

replayRoute(uint64,uint64,uint8[]).notice: The plaintext twin of the raid loop, so anyone can check a revealed raid.

retire(uint256).notice: Closes a vault, refunds unlooted stashes and opens the whole history for decryption.

revealHandles(uint256).notice: Handles to decrypt for `verifyReveal`, in the exact order the proof must cover.

scan(uint256,uint8,bool).notice: Privately asks whether a 3x3 area around `center` holds a trap or a live stash.

vaultCount().notice: Number of vaults ever created. Vault ids run from 0 to vaultCount - 1.

verifyReveal(uint256,bytes,bytes).notice: Checks the decryption proof, then replays every raid in plaintext and reverts unless         each one matches what the encrypted computation produced at the time.

userdoc.notice: Booby-trap a vault and log off. Raiders run routes against traps that only the         chain can evaluate, and nobody sees a trap that does not fire.
